results.title: Evidence-based literature review: De-duplication a cornerstone for quality
results.content: In 2016, an international research team led by Erasmus MC-Erasmus University Medical Centre in Rotterdam developed a de-duplication method (colloquially referred to as the Bramer method) for de-duplicating database search results in EndNote, a popular reference manager, which is used by information professionals conducting exhaustive searches for systematic reviews[[19](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10789108/#B19)]. In 2021, Canadian researchers evaluated the accuracy and efficiency of commonly used electronic methods for flagging and removing duplicate references in systematic reviews[[21](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10789108/#B21)]. The algorithm’s transparent and explainable decision process, along with its reproducibility and adherence to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) standards[[23](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10789108/#B23)], makes it a reliable tool for duplicate removal. doi: 10.1186/s12911-016-0280-9
